claim: Calibration is a conditional property that depends on the information retained by a predictor; proper-loss decomposition gives reliability, grouping (information loss), and irreducible uncertainty terms.
scope_conditions: Abstract page; full text in the html note
quoted_support: Calibration is a conditional property that depends on the information retained by a predictor.

breadth.confidence_families: Generic probabilistic classifier scores S=s(X) under proper losses (Brier, log-loss) (Sec 2-3)
breadth.benchmarks: Synthetic experiments and GermanCredit (logistic regression vs random forest, averaging and stacking) only
breadth.calibration_metrics: Population identities: proper-regret (reliability), grouping term (information loss X to S), irreducible uncertainty (Thm 2.1-2.6, Def 3.1, Prop 3.2); synthetic plus GermanCredit case study (Sec 5)
breadth.granularity: Instance-level classifier probabilities; information levels A subset B
